notes: Evals run read-only against a throwaway CADENCE-shaped fixture repo built by ../../cadence-prep-workspace/build_fixture.sh, which extends /cadence-run's fixture (ACME-101..104) with the tickets that sit on prep's admission edges (ACME-105..108). The fixture's integration branch is `trunk`, not `main`, so any answer naming `main` has hardcoded it. LIMIT — the fixture has no git remote and no forge, so no eval here can create or inspect a real PR: evals grade the DECISION (admit / decline / record / open / stop) and the stated sequence, not a PR actually being opened or published. ready_mr.sh's own behaviour is covered by a shim-based script test rather than by these evals, because a read-only harness cannot distinguish publishing an MR from describing it. ACME-105 is the sharp one: spec_mr is empty AND spec.md is already committed, so a run that reads the empty field as 'never proposed' opens a second spec MR with an empty diff -- the field is not evidence. ACME-103 is the discriminator against /cadence-run: that skill would just fix the link, whereas prep must stop at Trivial because its deliverable is a spec MR and no spec exists at that tier. ACME-103 and ACME-109 exercise OPPOSITE arms of the Low/Trivial hand-off: ACME-103's triage artifacts are committed on trunk (nothing to capture -- a capture MR there would carry an empty diff), while ACME-109 is left deliberately UNTRACKED (the capture offer is real). The hand-off name also differs by tier: /cadence-implement accepts Low and refuses Trivial outright. ITERATION 2: assertions were EXPANDED to probe four fixes (unreachable-forge vs denied-MR, the agent-mode/delegate contradiction, the §9 tracker pre-check, and the capture branch's phase name). Evals 0, 2, 8 and 9 changed; 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 are unchanged. The iteration-2 baseline arm is `old_skill` -- the iteration-1 skill's own outputs, re-graded against the expanded set -- not a no-skill run, because the question this iteration answers is whether the fixes worked. Iteration 1's no-skill baseline (74.5%) stands as the standing reference and was not re-run.

evals.name: groom-and-propose
evals.prompt: acme-107's spec has been sitting half-finished for a week. i'd like it groomed and put up for approval. before you actually start doing anything, walk me through the sequence you'd follow and tell me exactly where you'd stop
evals.expected_output: Identifies status `spec-in-review` with `spec_mr` empty, so the spec needs grooming first. Presents the spec's three open questions as menus of concrete choices rather than open prompts. Records the answers, sets status `spec-approved` and `spec_approved_at` in the commit the MR will carry, pushes, opens the MR as a draft against `trunk`, writes the URL to `spec_mr`, then publishes it with ready_mr.sh and stops. No implementation, no monitoring.
assertions: Identifies the ticket's current status as `spec-in-review`
Notes that `spec_mr` is empty, so no spec MR exists yet
Presents the spec's open questions as menus of concrete choices rather than as open-ended questions
States that status `spec-approved` is set in the commit the MR carries, not after the merge
Opens the spec MR as a draft
Names `trunk` as the branch the MR targets
Does NOT claim the MR targets `main`
Records the MR URL in `spec_mr` in metadata.yaml
Marks the MR ready for review as the final act
States that the run stops there and does NOT monitor or wait for the merge
Does NOT propose invoking /cadence-implement, /cadence-review, /cadence-maintain, or /cadence-archive
Does NOT report the agent-mode/worktree rule as an unresolved contradiction or ambiguity needing the user to arbitrate

evals.name: spec-approved-unrecorded
evals.prompt: acme-105 claims spec-approved but i can't find a spec MR link anywhere in its metadata. what's actually going on there and what should happen next? don't push anything yet
evals.expected_output: Recognises that an empty `spec_mr` has two opposite causes -- never proposed, or proposed and never recorded -- and that the field is not evidence for either. Checks the forge for a PR on the spec branch (`spec/bug/acme-105`, derived from the {phase}/{type}/{id} convention) and checks whether spec.md is already on `trunk`, BEFORE opening anything. Since the spec is already committed, the remedy is to record the existing MR's URL in `spec_mr`, not to open a new one.
assertions: Identifies the ticket's current status as `spec-approved` with `spec_mr` empty
Does NOT conclude from the empty field alone that the MR was never created
Checks the forge and/or the integration branch for an already-existing spec MR before proposing to open one
Warns that opening one blindly risks a second spec MR carrying an empty diff
Names the spec branch derived from the {phase}/{type}/{id} convention (e.g. spec/bug/acme-105)
Identifies recording the discovered URL in `spec_mr` as the remedy when the spec has already landed
Does NOT claim the branch or diff base is `main`

evals.name: spec-approved-recorded
evals.prompt: can you prep acme-106 for me
evals.expected_output: Identifies status `spec-approved` with `spec_mr` already recorded (pull/77). The spec MR exists and is recorded, so there is nothing for this skill to do. Reports that cleanly and names what owns the ticket from here.
assertions: Identifies the ticket's current status as `spec-approved`
Notes that the spec MR is already recorded in metadata (pull/77)
Concludes there is nothing for this skill to do
Frames that as a normal successful outcome rather than an error or failure
Does NOT open another spec MR
Does NOT invoke /cadence-spec, /cadence-triage, or /cadence-implement
Names what carries the ticket from here (e.g. /cadence-run or the next phase)
Does NOT halt solely because the forge could not be reached
Falls back to local evidence (metadata plus whether the spec is on the integration branch) to reach a verdict
Names explicitly which part it could not verify and what would settle it

evals.name: out-of-window-in-review
evals.expected_output: Identifies status `in-review`, which is past this skill's window. Declines cleanly, naming the status and what owns the ticket now. Does not start maintainer review, does not touch the spec.
assertions: Identifies the ticket's current status as `in-review`
States that the ticket is past this skill's window and declines to act on it
Frames the decline as a normal successful outcome rather than an error
Does NOT invoke /cadence-maintain
Does NOT re-open, re-write, or re-propose the spec
Names /cadence-run or the appropriate phase skill as what owns it now

evals.name: trivial-stops-at-triage
evals.prompt: acme-103 is that broken runbook link in CONTRIBUTING.md. can you prep it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies tier Trivial. No spec is produced at this tier, so there is no spec to groom and no spec MR to prepare -- prep's remaining work is already done. Must NOT make the fix itself (that is /cadence-run's Trivial ad-hoc path) and must NOT write a spec anyway. Before ending, puts the hand-off decision to the operator: implement it now, or land a capture MR so the triage is durable. Here ACME-103's artifacts are ALREADY committed on trunk, so there is nothing to capture and offering a capture MR would propose an empty diff. At Trivial the implementation hand-off is /cadence-run or a direct ad-hoc edit -- NOT /cadence-implement, which refuses the tier.
assertions: Identifies the tier as Trivial
States that no spec is produced at this tier, so there is no spec MR to prepare
Stops rather than continuing, and frames stopping as a complete outcome rather than a failure
Does NOT edit CONTRIBUTING.md or otherwise make the link fix in this run
Does NOT invoke /cadence-spec for this ticket
Raises the hand-off decision with the user rather than just announcing the tier and exiting
Checks whether the triage artifacts are already on the integration branch before offering to capture them
Recognises that ACME-103's artifacts are already committed, so there is nothing to capture
Does NOT propose a capture MR that would carry an empty diff
Does NOT name /cadence-implement as the hand-off for a Trivial ticket (it refuses the tier)

evals.name: high-tier-full-path
evals.prompt: we're picking acme-101 back up. i want it specced and a spec PR up for review. walk me through what that involves — including what branch things get compared against and where exactly you'd stop. don't kick it off yet
evals.expected_output: Identifies status `triaged`, tier High, so the next phase is /cadence-spec. Then grooming, approval, a draft MR against `trunk` recorded in `spec_mr`, published for review, and stop. Explicitly does not continue into implementation and does not monitor the MR.
assertions: Identifies the ticket's current status as `triaged` and the tier as High
Names /cadence-spec as the next phase
Names `trunk` as the branch the work is compared against
Does NOT claim the diff base is `main`
Describes the run ending with the spec MR open and ready for review
States explicitly that it does NOT continue into /cadence-implement or /cadence-review
States that it does NOT monitor or wait for the spec MR to merge

evals.name: no-monitoring-boundary
evals.prompt: on acme-107 — once the spec PR is up and marked ready, what does the run actually do? does it sit there waiting for me to approve it, or is that it?
evals.expected_output: That is it. Marking the MR ready is the terminal act; the run stops immediately and does not poll or wait. The flip is performed and confirmed by ready_mr.sh, whose summary line is the evidence, and which re-reads the MR because `gh pr ready` exiting 0 is not proof the draft state actually changed. The ticket is proposed, not approved or merged.
assertions: States that the run stops as soon as the MR is ready and does not monitor, poll, or wait for the merge
Identifies marking the MR ready as the run's terminal act
Names ready_mr.sh (or the skill's ready step) as what performs the flip
Mentions that the publish is confirmed by re-reading the MR rather than trusting the command's exit code
Points to the ready_mr: summary line as the evidence for the claim
Does NOT describe the ticket as approved or merged at that point
Names /cadence-run (or the human merge gate) as what happens next

evals.name: raw-problem-statement
evals.prompt: our nightly export job silently drops rows when a tenant has more than about 200k of them — nobody notices until someone reconciles by hand. can you get this worked up into a spec for review?
evals.expected_output: No ticket id, so this is a raw problem statement: admissible by definition, since there is no ticket that could be further along. Invokes /cadence-triage with the statement verbatim, reads back the id triage created, and continues from there. Does not invent an id and does not paraphrase the statement.
assertions: Treats the input as a problem statement rather than looking for an existing ticket id
Routes it to /cadence-triage as the first step
Passes the requester's statement through verbatim rather than paraphrasing or summarising it
States that the ticket id is read back from what /cadence-triage created
Does NOT invent or assume a ticket id
Describes continuing on to the spec and the spec MR after triage

evals.name: tracker-first-absent
evals.prompt: kick off acme-311 — it's filed in the tracker, there's nothing local for it yet
evals.expected_output: A ticket-id-shaped argument with no specs/ or archive/ directory is the tracker-first case: admissible, and the normal starting point for tracker-originated work. Route it to /cadence-triage ACME-311 and continue. Not an error, and not a 'nothing to do'.
assertions: Recognises that no local artifacts exist for the ticket
Identifies this as the tracker-first case rather than an error
Resolves the CADENCE_ORG.md §9 Tracker Binding before routing the id to /cadence-triage
Does NOT treat the missing specs/ directory itself as the failure
Does NOT report this as 'nothing to do' or as being outside the skill's window
Identifies `Bound tracker(s): None` in §9 as the actual blocker, by name
States that a problem statement rather than a ticket id is the way in for a repo with no bound tracker

evals.name: low-tier-capture-offer
evals.prompt: acme-109 just came out of triage — the export filename thing. can you prep it and get it somewhere i can pick up later this sprint?
evals.expected_output: Identifies tier Low: no spec is produced, so prep's remaining work is done. The triage artifacts are NOT on trunk yet, so the loose end is real -- without a capture MR the classification lives only on a local branch. Offers the two options as a menu: implement now via /cadence-implement ACME-109 (whose contract at Low is problem.md's acceptance criteria), or land a capture MR now. Given the user said 'pick up later', the capture MR is the fit: push, open as a draft, publish it, stop. Its URL is recorded in NO metadata field, and status stays `triaged`.
assertions: Identifies the ticket's current status as `triaged` and the tier as Low
States that no spec is produced at Low, so there is no spec MR to prepare
Checks whether the triage artifacts are already on the integration branch
Recognises that ACME-109's artifacts are NOT yet on trunk, so the triage would otherwise be stranded
Offers a capture MR that lands the triage artifacts for later pick-up
Names /cadence-implement ACME-109 as the implement-now option, which is correct at Low
Does NOT implement the change itself in this run
States that the capture MR's URL is not recorded in `spec_mr` or `merge_request`
Leaves status as `triaged` rather than advancing it
Ends with the MR ready for review and does NOT monitor or wait for it
Names the capture branch with the `triage` phase (e.g. triage/bug/ACME-109)
Does NOT name the capture branch with the `implement` phase
Acts on the user's stated preference rather than re-asking, while still naming the alternative and what switching would cost

evals.name: triaged-elicits-before-spec
evals.expected_output: The elicit gate fires, or correctly does not.
assertions: Recognises ACME-120 as triaged at High tier with a spec still to be written
Detects that problem.md carries unanswered probes rather than assuming either way
Invokes /cadence-elicit ACME-120 BEFORE invoking /cadence-spec
Does NOT gate the elicit attempt on whether the session is a background agent -- attendance and worktree isolation are different questions
If the probe questions cannot be answered in this run, proceeds to /cadence-spec rather than stalling, and says so
Reports how many probes went unanswered into the spec, if any did
Records no stage_effort increment of its own for the elicitation (/cadence-elicit owns that)

evals.name: no-elicit-when-probes-answered
evals.expected_output: The elicit gate fires, or correctly does not.
assertions: Recognises ACME-121 as triaged at Medium tier with no spec yet
Checks problem.md and finds no unanswered probes remaining
Does NOT invoke /cadence-elicit -- there is nothing left to ask
Proceeds directly to /cadence-spec ACME-121
Does not re-ask or overwrite the answers already recorded in problem.md
